column1: #   On 2026-08-28, Ashlar.Commercial.Tests.Fleet.Host was found to be in no solution,
#   named by no gate script, and absent from Ashlar.sln. Its four tests had been failing
#   for at least ten days across twenty consecutive runs of a manual-first weekly gate,
#   and no pull request had ever run them. Membership in a solution looked like coverage
#   TestOwnershipConventionTests asserts that every csproj containing Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk
#   has exactly one row here. That test lives in the Ashlar.Tests.Infrastructure.Tests.
#   Certification namespace, which is what cert-gate selects - one of five required status
#   checks on master. So a new test project that is not registered here cannot merge.
#   runner   the gate, script or workflow that executes it, or UNOWNED
#   expires  YYYY-MM-DD for UNOWNED rows (the date the debt must be resolved); "-" otherwise
#   note     why, in a few words
#   UNOWNED means: no pull-request check runs this project's tests. It is a dated debt,
#   not a permanent state. The list may shrink; adding to it needs a reason.
# ON PICKING AN EXPIRY DATE — read this before you set one.
#   and it runs inside cert-gate, one of five required status checks on master. An expiry that
#   passes therefore blocks EVERY pull request in the repository, with no code change and no
#   warning, on a date chosen months earlier. That is a scheduled outage, not a ratchet.
#   The first version of this file used 2026-10-27 — sixty days out — for seven rows at once.
#   Re-dated to 2027-03-31 on 2026-08-28, before anything tripped, per the rule below. Prefer
#   dates that are generous and STAGGERED: seven rows expiring on one day is one bad morning,
#   the same seven spread across months is seven small nudges.
#   The pressure this file applies should come from the weekly review, not from a cliff.
# The runner column is CHECKED SYNTAX (TestOwnershipRunnerConventionTests, cert-gate): every runner is
# UNOWNED or a real gate name, expires is "-" when gated. Still NOT proof a gate runs the project.

Run by changes to the code it guards, as of 2026-09-30: src/Ashlar.Manifest/**, src/Ashlar.Policies.Dev/**, src/Ashlar.Certification.Contracts/** and src/Ashlar.Analyzers/** were added to BOTH readiness path lists alongside src/Ashlar.Tests.Kernel/**, so editing GateStore.cs or AdmissionGate.cs now re-runs these 412 cases; before that it did not. Those four are the kernel project's transitive ProjectReference closure that no entry covered; the wider absent set (41 dirs across all 22 discovered suites, these four included) is closed as of 2026-09-30: the other 37 directories, plus the closure's implicit and cross-directory build inputs, are in BOTH readiness path lists, and ReadinessClosureConventionTests (cert-gate) recomputes the closure from the tree, including references declared in shared MSBuild files, and fails naming any directory or input that either list misses. It does not trace files read through MSBuild property functions. The sweep prints no per-project count; since 2026-09-30 an unfiltered sweep fails a discovered project that executes zero tests (ValidationServiceAdapter.ZeroExecutionError), but that floor is one executed test, not these 412, and readiness-summary counts a skipped lane as a pass: a lane, not a receipt.
